finding_resolutions.explanation: GDD Section 5 - Six-Week Development Plan (verified verbatim against Docs/GDD/No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md) states a schedule-risk fallback policy: stretch features are cut first, advanced door visuals/one encounter variation may be reduced next, the core required systems (three spells, two enemy types, door loop, mana regeneration, pursuit, final escape) are never cut, and if Weeks 5-6 required work overruns the fallback is to reduce final-room encounter density toward the low end of the 3-8 range and simplify presentation polish rather than cutting required systems. This is a development-process/prioritization invariant governing how the project team responds to schedule slippage, not a distinct executable feature, an acceptance criterion of one work item, or a delivery artifact. Per the requirement-representation repair policy this maps to requirement_type=pipeline_constraint. Added as a new non_code_requirements record titled 'Six-Week schedule fallback and required-scope protection' rather than creating a new work item.
